about: Viña Zorzal is run by the Sanz brothers, Xabi, Iñaki and Mikel, in southern Navarra, where their father Antonio started making his own wines in 1989. After founding Viña Zorzal in 2007, the brothers found very old, abandoned Garnacha vineyards in the hills of Fitero, near the Aragón border, and that discovery turned the winery toward single-vineyard wines. Malayeto is one of these: a named plot rather than a blend of the estate’s fruit.

The 2.39-hectare vineyard sits at about 520 metres at the foot of the mountains, on the same slope as Zorzal’s Corral de los Altos, in rocky clay and limestone. The bush vines are around forty years old and farmed organically without tilling, using native cover crops and compost. Wine Advocate reports the 2021 was fermented in stainless steel and concrete and matured about a year in used 500-litre barrels and a large oak foudre, then bottled in February 2023, about 13,300 bottles in all.

Fitero’s continental climate of hot days, cold nights and stony ground gives a fresher, more mountain style of Garnacha than the flat, high-yielding vineyards elsewhere in Navarra. Luis Gutiérrez of Wine Advocate scored the 2021 at 94 points, and reviewers describe blackberry, black pepper and mint in a supple, medium-bodied frame. It should drink well through 2030.
facts: Single 2.39 ha plot in Fitero, about 520 m; vines around 40 years old
About 1 year in used 500 L barrels and an oak foudre (per Wine Advocate)
